analysis.title: BofA Securities Equity Client Flow Trends: Clients buy the dip (with ETFs)
key_insights: In the week of 11/2-11/6, with the S&P 500 down 2.7% (biggest weekly decline since April 2025), BofA clients bought US equities after 3 weeks of outflows. Net buys were +$4.9bn in total, led by equity ETFs (+$5.3bn, 4th largest ever) against single stock outflows (-$0.4bn, 4th straight week of outflows).

Institutional clients led the buying (+$6.1bn) after outsized selling in October. Hedge funds bought equities for the first time in 4 weeks (+$0.8bn). Private clients sold equities for the 4th straight week (-$2.1bn).
Clients bought large cap equities (+$4.9bn) and sold mid cap (-$0.5bn) and small and micro cap (-$0.04bn) on a stocks plus ETFs basis.

Corporate client buybacks slowed last week. Annualized YTD buybacks are tracking below 2024-25 levels but above 2010-23 annual levels. Rolling 52-week buybacks as a share of S&P 500 market cap are 0.18%, the lowest since August 2021, down from a 0.42% peak in February 2025.

Clients sold stocks in 5 of the 11 sectors. Industrials had the largest single stock outflow (-$2.0bn) and the longest sell streak, 15 weeks (longest on record is 30 weeks in 2016). BofA's short-term Momentum & Value model ranks Industrials among the worst sectors.
Energy single stock outflows were the biggest since June and the first in 4 weeks (-$0.7bn), as oil prices fell.

Financials had the largest sector inflows (+$1.6bn in single stocks), the 4th largest in history, or 1.3 standard deviations above the mean when normalized by market cap. Clients also bought Tech (+$0.7bn, first time in 4 weeks) and sold Communication Services (-$0.7bn, 4th straight week) in roughly offsetting amounts.

Equity ETF inflows spanned all major styles (Value, Blend, Growth) and all size segments. 7 of 11 sector ETFs saw inflows, led by Financials (+$182mn) and Tech (+$173mn). Industrials ETFs had the biggest outflows (-$158mn). Blend ETFs were the largest style inflow (+$3.9bn).
Year to date, clients have sold single stocks (-$105.6bn) and bought equity ETFs (+$70.8bn), for a net -$34.8bn. YTD corporate buybacks are $93.3bn.

By client type YTD: hedge funds net bought single stocks (+$14.2bn) and ETFs (+$5.3bn). Institutional clients net sold single stocks (-$61.6bn) and bought ETFs (+$27.4bn). Private clients net sold single stocks (-$58.3bn) and bought ETFs (+$38.1bn).
Rolling 4-week average total US equity flows are -$3.2bn per the Exhibit 4 title. The total 4-week average from the weekly table is -$1.6bn.

Rolling 4-week average trends: institutional single stock outflows for the 7th straight week, but institutional equity (stock plus ETF) flows flipped positive. Hedge fund single stock outflows for the 4th straight week. Large cap equity outflows for the 7th straight week. Tech single stock outflows for the 6th week.

ETF flow z-scores for the latest week: total ETF flows 2.38 vs the 3-month history. Institutional equity ETF z-score is 1.74 and private client equity ETF z-score is 2.47. Hedge funds were slight net sellers of equity ETFs (z-score -0.14).

Among sector ETFs, Energy ETFs have had 4-week average inflows for the 8th straight week, as have Health Care and Utilities ETFs. Financials ETFs had 4-week average inflows for the first time since early August.
Exhibit 17 weekly sector flow z-scores vs the past 5 years: Financials +2.53, Utilities +2.38, Industrials -3.03, Energy -1.52, Health Care -1.18.

Largest sector inflows last week (+$1.6bn in single stocks), 4th largest in history. The 5-year flow z-score is +2.53. This describes client flow, not a BofA rating.
Largest outflows since June (-$0.7bn single stocks) as oil prices fell, though Energy ETFs have had 8 straight weeks of 4-week average inflows.
Clients bought Tech for the first time in 4 weeks (+$0.7bn single stocks), while the 4-week average single stock flow remains negative for the 6th week.

risk_factors: Buyback support is fading: rolling 52-week buybacks as a share of S&P 500 market cap are the lowest since August 2021.
Single stock selling persists. Total single stock flows were negative for the 4th straight week, and the 4-week average is -$5.7bn.
The weekly flow data is influenced by block trades and is more volatile than the 4-week average, per the methodology note.

vol_and_positioning: Clients bought equity ETFs of +$5.3bn last week, the 4th largest weekly ETF inflow ever, during the S&P 500's biggest weekly decline since April 2025.
Hedge funds bought equities (+$0.8bn) for the first time in 4 weeks, but their 4-week average single stock flow is still negative (-$1.4bn), with outflows for the 4th straight week.
Private clients are net sellers of equities for the 4th straight week and have had 4-week average equity outflows since early August.
Industrials have the longest client sell streak at 15 weeks, against a record 30 weeks in 2016.
Large cap equities have had 4-week average outflows for the 7th straight week.

tension_points.bull_case: Clients bought $4.9bn of US equities after 3 weeks of outflows, led by institutional clients and a record-scale ETF inflow, with hedge funds also buying for the first time in 4 weeks.
